description: GhostDAG data of small DAGs under the rules at/after the hardening activation (reference/gnb_ghostdag.py; docs/CONSENSUS.md, "Coloring" and "Parent list"). Blocks are inserted in the listed order; ids are 32-byte hex; works, heights, scores and blue works are decimal strings. `mergeset_order` is the normative candidate order (FIFO Kahn, ids ascending among the blocks a step makes ready). A block whose `expected` is an `error` is refused and not inserted.

cases.description: Audit B2-T9. k = 10. B's parents are its selected parent sp (the heaviest), T2..T11 and U; T1..T11 and sp are children of P, U is a child of T1. The mergeset is T1..T11 and U. U has the lowest id but becomes ready only when T1 is taken, so GnB's FIFO order is T1..T11, U: blues T1..T10, reds T11 and U. The other reading (always the lowest ready id) gives T1, U, T2..T11: blues T1, U, T2..T9 and a different blue work (`alternative_reading`). B's header height (4) also differs from its DAG height (3): U has DAG height 3.

alternative_reading.reading: lowest ready id first (NOT GnB's rule)

cases.description: Audit B2-T10. D1 lists the merged parent C twice, D2 the selected parent A twice, D3 neither: their GhostDAG data are identical (the DAG treats the parent list as a set). The header rule `duplicate_parents` is the verdict from the hardening activation: a block with a repeated parent is invalid at or after it (`block_rules::check_parents_distinct`) and valid below it.

Audit B2-T10. X merges the chain A1..A3 under the heavier selected parent H, so X has DAG height 2 but header height 4. R lists X and A3, which is already in X's past; R2 lists X only. A redundant ancestor is valid at every height: it is never the selected parent and adds nothing to the mergeset (R and R2 have the same GhostDAG data), but the header height is taken over every listed parent, so R's header height is 4 and R2's is 3.

The mergeset-size limit, this chain's rule at every height: at most 64 blocks merged besides the selected parent (MERGESET_SIZE_LIMIT; tighter than the audit's hardened MAX_MERGESET_SIZE - 1 = 179). S1..S66 are children of G, S1 the heaviest. BIG lists all 66 (65 merged): refused with MergesetTooLarge and not inserted. OK lists S1..S65 (64 merged): accepted; with k = 10, 10 of the 64 are blue.
